name: Wall calf stretch
summary: Gastrocnemius (straight knee) or soleus (bent knee) stretch, verified heel-down and knee-correct.
setup: Stand facing a wall with both hands on it, side-on to the camera at hip height, 2–3 m away. Step the stretching leg back so it is the leg nearest the camera; toes pointing at the wall. Whole body from hands to back heel in frame.
brief: Stand facing a wall with both hands on it. Step the stretching leg back, toes pointing at the wall, and press that heel down until the calf pulls.
why: Side-on, the three things that make or break the stretch — back heel on the floor, back knee straight or bent, shin leaning toward the wall — are each a direct height or angle read.

guide.surface: Wall or doorframe. Barefoot or in flat shoes. Non-slip floor.

points.t: Both palms flat on the wall at shoulder height, shoulder-width apart, arms nearly straight with a soft elbow.
Lean by bending the elbows slightly and moving the hips toward the wall — the arms guide, they do not push.
Stepped straight back, toes pointing directly at the wall — not turned out. Heel flat on the floor and pressed down throughout.
Foot in line with its hip, not crossed behind the body; hip-width from the front foot.
Straight-knee (calf) variant: back knee fully straight. Bent-knee (soleus) variant: back knee softly bent 20–40°, heel still down.
Front foot flat, toes at the wall, about 30 cm from it. Front knee bends as you lean and stays over the front foot, not past it.
Hips square to the wall, both hip bones the same distance from it. Move the hips forward as one unit; do not push one side forward.
Lean from the ankle, not by folding at the waist — shoulders, hips and back ankle form one straight line.
Spine long and neutral, chest up, shoulders down and relaxed.
Eyes on the wall in front of you, chin level.

Ease in until you feel a firm pull in the calf (straight knee) or lower toward the Achilles (bent knee), never pain. Breathe slowly; on each breath out, see if the hips can come a little further forward.
Hold 20–60 s, 2–3 times per side, ideally after a warm-up or at the end of a walk.

guide.stop: Sharp pain in the Achilles or the arch, or if the heel cannot stay down without pain — shorten the step instead.

enterCue: Hands on the wall, step the back leg back, and lean in
tempo: Ease in over 3 s, hold, breathe.
dosage: 3 × 30 s each leg, once or twice a day.
progression: Step the back foot further away; the bent-knee variant for the soleus.
regression: Step closer to the wall; hands higher.
contraindications: Sharp calf or Achilles pain, or a recent calf tear.

faults.label: Back heel lifting
faults.tip: The stretch only reaches the calf when the heel stays flat. Step the foot closer to the wall if it will not stay down.

faults.label: Back knee bending
faults.tip: For the calf (gastrocnemius) stretch the back knee must stay straight; a bent knee shifts the stretch to the soleus.

faults.label: Back knee not bent enough
faults.cue: Bend the back knee a little more
faults.tip: For the soleus variant keep the back knee softly bent, about 20–40°.

faults.label: Not leaning in enough
faults.cue: Lean in until you feel the calf
faults.tip: Move the hips toward the wall; the shin should tilt forward at least 10–15°.

faults.label: Hands not at shoulder height
faults.cue: Hands on the wall at shoulder height
faults.tip: Hands too high pull the shoulders up and arch the back; too low folds you at the waist.

faults.label: Hands too low on the wall
faults.tip: Hands too high pull the shoulders up and arch the back; too low folds you at the waist.

faults.label: Front knee straight
faults.cue: Bend the front knee as you lean
faults.tip: The front knee bends toward the wall so the hips can travel forward; a straight front leg blocks the lean.

faults.label: Bending at the hips
faults.cue: Keep your body in a straight line
faults.tip: Lean from the ankle, not the waist — shoulders, hips and back knee in one line.
